source.section: Schedule 2 line 11 code 601 and PDF pages 19-20 Civil Service Annuity Deduction, with its examples ('all amounts of Social Security income'); Schedule 3 line 1 (PDF page 24: joint 2,000, all other filers 1,000), line 4 (PDF page 25: 1,000 age 65 or older), line 5 (PDF page 25: 500 age 65 or older and IT-40 line 1 under 40,000, or under 20,000 married filing separately); Form IT-40 lines 1-8 (PDF page 1; line 8 'multiply line 7 by 3% (.03)'); booklet PDF page 8 Line 1; PDF pages 5-6 rounding

worked: Federal AGI = federal civil service annuity person 0 24,000.00 + taxable Social Security 2,500.00 = 26,500.00. Social Security received: person 0 12,000.00; the federal taxable amount from the federal worksheet is 2,500.00. Federal taxable income = 26,500.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 8,750.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored; Indiana starts from federal AGI). Form IT-40 line 1 federal AGI 26,500.00. Line 2 add-backs 0.00; line 3 = 26,500.00 + 0.00 = 26,500.00. Civil service annuity person 0 (age 67): cap 16,000.00 less that person's own Social Security received 12,000.00 and railroad retirement 0.00 = 4,000.00; lesser of the annuity 24,000.00 and 4,000.00 = 4,000.00. Schedule 2: line 5 taxable Social Security 2,500.00; line 11 code 601 civil service annuity 4,000.00; line 12 total = 6,500.00. IT-40 line 4 = 6,500.00. Line 5 = 26,500.00 - 6,500.00 = 20,000.00. Schedule 3: line 1 1,000.00; line 4 1 x 1,000.00 = 1,000.00; line 5 IT-40 line 1 26,500.00 is under 40,000.00: 1 x 500.00 = 500.00; line 7 total = 2,500.00. IT-40 line 6 = 2,500.00. Line 7 = 20,000.00 - 2,500.00 = 17,500.00. Line 8 = 17,500.00 x 0.03 = 525.00. No credits; county tax (line 9) is local and out of scope. State income tax 525.00. The cap is reduced by all Social Security received (12,000.00), not the federal taxable part (2,500.00). The annuity is over 16,000, so booklet and projection agree.
